definitions.K0_GRAPH: maximum number of resident recruitment events along any branch before no outgoing front remains, when no reachable transmitting cycle exists
definitions.NONTRANSMITTING_ZERO: no outgoing front capable of recruiting another previously nonresponding resident
definitions.TRANSMITTING: canonical relay state has at least one exact outgoing front that can reach and recruit the next homogeneous resident
definitions.TRANSMITTING_CYCLE: reachable directed cycle consisting only of transmitting states

path_level_annotation: BRANCHING_MIXED is a third survival/multiplicity class but does not create a third causal-support alternative beyond recurrent-cycle-present versus all-branches-eventually-zero.
scope: homogeneous cyclic aligned carrier; stationary N/q/time-independent local relay rule; finite controller-relevant canonical relay-front quotient; CPBC keeps every allowed action branch
stage_g_application: rho_G is a one-vertex transmitting self-loop, hence falls in the recurrent/system-spanning side.
theorem_support_level: If a reachable transmitting cycle exists, at least one exact CPBC branch can repeat the canonical cycle through arbitrarily many homogeneous sites; causal-support union is system-spanning on every nondegenerate finite N.

If no reachable transmitting cycle exists, the transmitting portion of the finite graph is acyclic after SCC condensation. Therefore K0_GRAPH is finite and RESPONSE_PARTICIPANT_COUNT_CLOSURE <= min(N,1+K0_GRAPH), independent of N.

If both recurrent and extinct branches are reachable, classify BRANCHING_MIXED at history level; causal-support closure is still system-spanning because the recurrent branch is retained, while not every history transmits.
